content.text:
**Recommendation: Sentry**, unless your app is mobile-first or you need the cheapest possible error-only tool.

I haven't checked current pricing or plan limits, and they change often, so confirm them on each vendor's pricing page before you buy.

| | **Sentry** | **Rollbar** | **Bugsnag** (SmartBear) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core focus | Errors plus performance tracing, session replay, profiling, cron monitoring, logs | Error tracking and grouping, with lighter performance features | Error and stability monitoring, strongest on mobile and release health |
| Language/SDK coverage | Broadest; most languages and frameworks | Good for common web and backend stacks | Good, especially for iOS, Android, and other mobile SDKs |
| Free tier | Yes, usable for a small team (limited users and events) | Yes, with a monthly event cap | Yes, with a monthly event cap |
| Pricing model | Base plan plus usage for errors, transactions, and replays. Can get complicated to forecast | Mainly per-event, which is simpler to predict | Per-event with seat-based plans. Check the seat terms |
| Release and regression tracking | Strong: suspect commits, source maps, release health | Solid | Strong, with stability scores per release |
| Integrations | Very broad: GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear, and more | Good core integrations | Good core integrations |
| Self-hosting | Yes (open source) | No | No |

**Why Sentry for a 10-person team:**
- The free tier is enough to start, and the paid plan covers a team of this size.
- It grows with you. If you later want performance tracing or session replay to debug issues, it's already there, so you don't need a second tool.
- It has the broadest integrations, so alerts can go to Slack and bugs can link to GitHub without extra glue.
- Self-hosting is an option if data residency becomes a requirement.

**When I'd choose otherwise:**
- **Bugsnag** if most of your users are on mobile apps and you care most about crash-free sessions and per-release stability.
- **Rollbar** if you only want error tracking, want the simplest setup, and prefer predictable per-event billing over a platform with more moving parts.

**What would change this:** your main stack, expected monthly event volume, whether you have mobile apps, and whether you need self-hosting or specific compliance terms. If you tell me those, I can narrow it down. I can also run a live search for current pricing and plan limits before you decide.
